newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador sees 10 pct sucre depreciation by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador sees 10 pct sucre depreciation by year-end.

text.p: Ecuador's sucre is expected to decreciate by between 10 and 11 percent against the dollar by the end of the year, a senior government official said Friday.

"Until the end of the year it is calculated that (the rate of depreciation) will be 10 or 11 percent, which means the dollar will be between 4,400 and 4,500 sucres," Danilo Carrera, head of the policy-setting Monetary Board, told reporters. That level implies the currency will depreciate by between 21 and 23.7 percent in 1997, while inflation this year is expected to come in between 28 and 30 percent.
The dollar is currently quoted at 4,043 sucres. It depreciated by 24.27 percent in 1996.
Ecuador has used a crawling peg currency system for the sucre against the dollar since 1994.
In March this year, the government of President Fabian Alarcon raised the rate of depreciation to 21 percent from 18.5 percent as originally forecast.

Central bank authorities recently announced that the rate of depreciation will be reduced to between 16 and 18 percent next year, which is seen compatible with inflation projected at 20 and 22 percent.
((--Franz Bastidas, Quito Newsroom, 5932 258429 e- mail: reuters1@reutersecu.com.ec))
